A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, framework, and core theorems. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated and removed content.

before.justification: Appendix G reports original synthetic GD/SGD experiments and MNIST training experiments, including divergence thresholds, test losses, and classification accuracies.

after.justification: Appendix G retains original synthetic GD/SGD simulations, with measured convergence behavior, divergence thresholds, and error bars.

M1.justification: Section 2.3 and Appendix C.2 change SGD's block candidate output from iterates p_0 through p_K0 to p_0 through p_(K0-1). This is a limited output revision. Gradient updates and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged; folding the separate output rule R into A2 is otherwise equivalent.

E1.justification: The entire MNIST classification study in v2 Appendix G.3 is removed, eliminating the only real-data neural-network evaluation. Both versions retain synthetic optimization of ||Aw||^p for p = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The added DRO discussion does not include an evaluation.

E2.justification: The retained studies use the same GD and SGD methods, with no added competing optimizers. The removed MNIST study varied activation configurations under SGD and did not introduce a separate optimizer comparator.

E3.justification: Removing Appendix G.3 removes a distinct neural-network evaluation protocol: 50 training epochs, batch size 64, ten learning rates, and test-loss and accuracy evaluation. The retained simulations preserve their 30 step sizes, 100 initializations, 1,000 iterations, and SGD noise specification.

E4.justification: The MNIST sensitivity study testing how ReLU powers 1–4 affect the stable learning-rate range disappears. The broader sensitivity investigations across initialization distributions and synthetic objective powers remain unchanged, making this a limited removal of complementary analysis.

E5.justification: MNIST's 50 random-test-slice evaluations per once-trained configuration and their ±2 standard-deviation reporting are removed. The synthetic studies retain 100 initializations and ±2 standard-deviation bars. There is no reported increase in runs or new significance testing.

E6.justification: All MNIST loss and accuracy results disappear, including Figure 11's ineffective-training thresholds of 0.359, 0.0464, 0.0167, and 0.00599 for powers 1–4. The synthetic results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–10 retain their values and trends; no comparable-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds the p_n <= 0 case, corrects an event label in the disjoint union, and expands the conditional-probability derivation. Remark 3 adds reasoning about step-size-search complexity. The principal assumptions, convergence-rate statements, and application proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central novelty and convergence-rate claims remain intact. Section 1.1 newly states applicability to distributionally robust optimization through the relationship with Xie et al. (2024), modestly extending the explicitly claimed application scope.

C2.justification: New Remarks 3–4 discuss using bounds on unknown initialization-dependent quantities, finding step sizes through binary search or cross-validation, and interpreting such tuning as adaptive. The MNIST-specific interpretation of activation power and training stability is removed; the analogous synthetic interpretation remains.

D1.justification: The MNIST deletion removes its 128-unit hidden-layer specification, PyTorch initialization details, training recipe, and two-A6000-GPU disclosure. Technical details and code-attachment statements for the retained synthetic simulations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lee et al. (2016, 2019) to distinguish asymptotic saddle avoidance and Gower et al. (2019, 2021) for expected smoothness. It also develops the DRO connection to the already-cited Xie et al. (2024), while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The central exposition is substantially reorganized: Section 2.1 separates two core insights, Section 2.2 introduces a deterministic special case before the general framework, and the separate R notation is removed throughout. v3 also adds explanatory remarks, separates practical implications into Section 3.7, and moves the contents after the references.

P2.justification: MNIST Figures 11–12 are removed, and retained displays are repositioned, including Table 1 moving above Figure 1. The ten synthetic figures and two tables retain their visual structure and content; remaining layout changes mainly reflect text reflow and contents relocation.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the framework easier to follow and adds useful research context and limited proof refinements. However, it removes the sole real-data validation and its uncertainty reporting, leaving practical evidence entirely synthetic while retaining broad practical claims. These expository gains and the loss of empirical breadth do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
